newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks trade firmer, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks trade firmer, seen consolidating.

text.p: Greek stocks were trading 0.42 percent higher early on Friday and market watchers said the market would consolidate around 1,400 points.

"The bourse is stabilising. We consider the 1,400 support level as satisfactory and foreign investors view this consolidation favourably," said John Tegopoulos, the head of research at Midland Pandelakis Securities.
Trading is narrow because banking shares are idle, he added.
"People invested in banks, are now either engaging in profit-taking or are holding their positions in view of more news from income statements," he said.
Investment interest is focused on stocks of companies with strong financial results, he added.
"The market is responding positively to good news. This will draw more conservative investors especially foreigners, to Greek equties," he said.
Subscriptions to Xiosbank's IPO started on Tuesday April 15 and end Friday April 18. The bank is going public at 2,650 drachmas a share seeking to raise 4.43 billion.
The Athens general share index was trading 0.42 percent or 5.95 points higher at 1,426.46 from Thursday's 1,420.51 close, after opening at 1,421.82.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 1,082.0-1,112.0. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were losing 15 drachmas, at 6,130.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $60.37-$62.06. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 1,078-2,169 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $12.63-$14.33. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
